title: The Conker
phrases: a pale round patch on top

doing.t: is peeping out of its split, spiky green case
is polished to a bright shine
is hanging from a knotted string
has a pale, dull patch on top

close: Just the conker, with its swirly brown grain and a bright shine.
Only the conker and its split green case, side by side.

roles.dark: for the dark grain lines and the shadow underneath
roles.light: for the shine
roles.accent: for the pale fawn patch on top

firstMark: Start with the shadow under the conker: a crescent of {dark}, pressed firmly.
Start with the grain in fine curved lines of {main}, leaving a patch of bare paper for the shine.

title: The Ring of Mushrooms

doing.t: has come up in a neat circle
has one mushroom just outside the circle
is made of dozens of flat, pale brown caps
has a gap where a few mushrooms have fallen over

close: Just the ring of mushrooms, seen from a little above so the circle shows.
Only one mushroom from the ring, tipped up to show the gills underneath.

roles.dark: for the shadow under each cap
roles.light: for the cream stems and undersides
roles.accent: for the green grass between the caps

firstMark: Start with a faint ring of {main} dots to mark out the circle.
Start with the shadow tucked under the nearest cap in {dark}.

title: The Red Toadstool
a: a red toadstool with white spots
the: the red toadstool with white spots
phrases: a white stem with a frill

doing.t: is still small and round, its spots close together
has opened out flat and wide
has a bite taken out of its cap
is leaning over, with a white frill round its stem

close: Just the toadstool, cap and stem, with all its white spots in place.
Only the toadstool, seen from low down so you can see under the cap.

roles.dark: for the shadow under the cap
roles.light: for the white spots and stem
roles.accent: for the orange edge of the cap

firstMark: Start with the spots: leave each one as a circle of bare paper and colour round them in {main}.
Start with the dark band under the cap in {dark}.

title: The Pinecone
phrases: a pale tip on each scale

doing.t: has opened every scale wide
has its scales shut tight
has a papery seed stuck between two scales
has white paint dabbed on every tip

close: Just the pinecone, seen from the side so the scales spiral round.
Only the pinecone, seen from underneath, with its scales in a spiral.

roles.dark: for the gaps between the scales
roles.light: for the pale tip of each scale
roles.accent: for the drops of sticky orange sap

firstMark: Start with the dark gaps between the scales: small wedges of {dark}, working round from the bottom.
Start with the outline of one scale near the middle in {main}, then build outwards.

title: The Rosehips

doing.t: are hanging in a shiny cluster from a thorny stem
are each tipped with a dry brown tuft
have gone soft, dark and wrinkled
have one hip pecked open by a bird

close: Just the rosehips, three or four on one stem.
Only one rosehip, big enough to fill the page.

roles.dark: for the stem, the thorns and the shady side of each hip
roles.light: for the shine on each hip
roles.accent: for the dry brown tuft at each tip

firstMark: Start with the shine: leave a small oval of bare paper on each hip and colour round it in {main}.
Start with the stem and its hooked thorns in {dark}, before any red goes down.

title: The Fern
phrases: rows of leaflets on each side

doing.t: is uncurling one tight green coil
has its feathery leaves spread wide
has one leaf much longer than the rest
has rows of brown dots under its leaves
has one leaf turned dry and brown

close: Just one fern leaf, from the stalk to the tip.
Only one new fern leaf, still curled up tight like a snail shell.

roles.dark: for the shade between the leaflets
roles.light: for the yellow-green tips
roles.accent: for the brown stalk at the bottom

firstMark: Start with the centre line of one leaf: a single curved line of {dark} from bottom to tip.
Start with the curl at the tip in {main}, drawn like a snail shell.

title: The Striped Pebble
a: a pebble with a white stripe
the: the pebble with a white stripe

doing.t: is wet and shiny
sits on top of two other pebbles
is lying beside two plain grey pebbles
has rusty orange specks beside its stripe

close: Just the pebble, with the white stripe running all the way round.
Only the pebble, life size, with its specks and its white stripe.

roles.dark: for the shadow underneath
roles.light: for the white stripe and the shine
roles.accent: for the rusty orange specks

firstMark: Start with the stripe: leave it as bare paper and colour each side of it in {main}.
Start with the shadow underneath: a flat oval of {dark} along the bottom edge.

title: The Sycamore Seeds
phrases: a papery wing on each seed
joined in pairs, like a V

doing.t: are still joined in pairs, wings spread wide
are hanging in a bunch from a twig
are lying in a heap
are spinning down through the air
have dried to a pale brown

close: Just one pair of sycamore seeds, wings spread wide.
Only three pairs of sycamore seeds in a row, from green to brown.

roles.dark: for the round seed at the end of each wing
roles.light: for the pale see-through edge of each wing
roles.accent: for the reddish lines along each wing

firstMark: Start with the seeds: a plump teardrop of {dark} at the end of each wing.
Start with the fine lines on each wing in {main}, fanning out from the seed.

title: The Foxgloves

doing.t: are standing tall in a row
have a bumblebee climbing out of the lowest bell
are leaning together, heavy with flowers
are open all the way to the top

close: Just one foxglove stem, from the lowest bell to the top bud.
Only one bell, big enough to see the spots inside.

roles.dark: for the deep inside of each bell
roles.light: for the pale lip of each bell
roles.accent: for the dark purple spots inside the bells

firstMark: Start with the open mouth of the lowest bell, a dark curve of {dark}.
Start with the outline of the lowest bell in {main}, then hang the others above it, each one a touch smaller.

title: The Blackberry Branch

doing.t: has some berries ripe and some still red
has one big ripe berry hanging at the end
is arching over in a long, thorny loop
has pale pink flowers and hard green berries
has leaves turning red at the edges

close: Just one blackberry branch with three berries at different stages.
Only one blackberry, near enough to count the bumps.

roles.dark: for the shadows between the bumps
roles.light: for the shine on each bump
roles.accent: for the red unripe berries

firstMark: Start with one blackberry: a cluster of small circles in {main}, each with a dot of bare paper for the shine.
Start with the thorns along the stem: hooked marks of {dark}.

title: The Snowdrops

doing.t: are hanging their heads in a clump
have opened their outer petals wide
have only just come up, still closed
are standing in an egg cup, three stems together

close: Just one snowdrop, near enough to see the green mark on the inner petals.
Only a clump of five snowdrops, seen from ground level.

roles.main: for the petals and their pale shadows
roles.dark: for the stems and the shade where the leaves cross
roles.light: for the brightest white on the petals
roles.accent: for the green mark inside each flower

firstMark: Start with the shadow side of each petal, the lightest touch of {dark}, and let the paper be the white.
Start with the stem in {dark}, arching over at the top like a hook.

title: The Bluebells
phrases: stems bent over at the top

doing.t: are bending over at the top of their stems
have a bee hanging upside down from one bell
are half open, more green than blue
have one stem bent right over by its bells

close: Just three bluebell stems, each one bending over at the tip.
Only one bluebell flower, with its petal tips curled back.

roles.dark: for the inside of each bell
roles.light: for the paler tips of the petals
roles.accent: for the green stems and leaves

firstMark: Start with the bend of the stem in {dark}, curving over at the top.
Start with the lowest bell, a small upside-down cup of {main}.

title: The Dandelion Clock
phrases: a fluffy white ball of seeds

doing.t: is still a perfect, fluffy white ball
has lost half its seeds
is standing tall on its stalk
has a few seeds floating away

close: Just the dandelion clock, a fluffy ball of seeds on one stalk.
Only one seed, drawn large, with its tuft of fine white hairs.

roles.main: for the pale grey of the fluffy ball
roles.dark: for the seeds packed in the middle
roles.light: for the fine white hairs
roles.accent: for the green stalk

firstMark: Start in the middle with a dome of close dots in {dark}, where the seeds are packed together.
Start with fine strokes of {main}, going out from the middle like the spokes of a wheel.

title: The Sunflower
phrases: as wide as a dinner plate

doing.t: is turned to face the light
has a ring of yellow petals round a dark middle
is still half closed, petals folded over the middle
is drooping on its stalk, heavy with seeds
has half its seeds pecked out by birds

close: Just the sunflower head, face on, with the seeds in curving rows.
Only the sunflower head, seen from the side, with its petals and the green back of the flower.

roles.dark: for the dark middle
roles.light: for the bright petal tips
roles.accent: for the green stalk

firstMark: Start with the middle: a big circle of {dark} dots in curving rows.
Start with one petal at the top in {main}, then work round like a clock face.

title: The Pumpkin

doing.t: is sitting round and squat, with a curly stalk
still has a curl of dry vine on its stalk
has a carved face and a candle inside
is in a row with two smaller pumpkins

close: Just the pumpkin, with the ribs curving round from the stalk.
Only the stalk and the top of the pumpkin, up close, with the ridges on the stalk.

roles.dark: for the grooves between the ribs
roles.light: for the shine across the top of each rib
roles.accent: for the dry brown stalk

firstMark: Start with the grooves: curved lines of {dark} running from the stalk to the base.
Start with the rib at the front in {main}, pressing harder towards its edges so it rounds out.

title: The Acorn

doing.t: is sitting snug in its cup
has its empty cup lying beside it
is still green and shiny, half in its cup
has split open and grown one pale root

close: Just the acorn in its knobbly cup, drawn twice life size.
Only the acorn and its cup, apart, side by side.

roles.dark: for the shadow in the cup and under the acorn
roles.light: for the shine on the nut
roles.accent: for the green tinge near the cup

firstMark: Start with the cup: rows of knobbly bumps in {dark}.
Start with the curved side of the acorn in {main}, leaving a long strip of bare paper for the shine.

title: The Oak Leaf

doing.t: is lying upside down with its veins showing
is curling up at the edges
is pressed flat between the pages of a book
has a few holes nibbled in it
is turning brown round the edges
is still hanging on its twig, dry and brown

close: Just the oak leaf, life size, with every wavy edge and vein.
Only the oak leaf, half green and half brown.

roles.dark: for the veins and the curled edges
roles.light: for the pale underside
roles.accent: for the patch of green near the stalk

firstMark: Start with the middle vein, one firm line of {dark} from stalk to tip.
Start with the wavy outline in {main}, one rounded bump at a time.

title: The Holly

doing.t: is covered in red berries
has one smooth leaf with no prickles
has leaves so shiny they look wet
has a tartan ribbon tied round its stem

close: Just the sprig of holly, three leaves and a cluster of berries.
Only one holly leaf, with all its prickly points.

roles.dark: for the shadows where the leaves overlap
roles.light: for the white shine on each leaf
roles.accent: for the red berries

firstMark: Start with the centre vein of each leaf in {dark}, then draw the prickly edges out from it.

title: The Ivy

has one long stem going off on its own
is spilling over the edge of its pot
has round green flower heads with bees on them
has bunches of black berries

close: Just one length of ivy, five leaves and the stem that joins them.
Only one ivy leaf, with its pale veins left as bare paper.

roles.dark: for the deepest shade and the berries
roles.light: for the pale veins
roles.accent: for the reddish-brown stem

firstMark: Start with the veins of one leaf: leave them as bare paper and colour between them in {main}.

title: The Mossy Stone

has a snail resting in the moss
has moss with thin stalks and brown tips

close: Just the mossy stone, with the moss drawn as hundreds of short strokes.
Only the top of the stone, where the moss is thickest.

roles.dark: for the shadow under the stone and down in the moss
roles.light: for the bright tips of the moss
roles.accent: for the grey stone where it shows through

firstMark: Start with the moss: lots of dots of {main}, packed close where it is thickest.
Start with the shadow at the base in {dark}, then work up the stone.

title: The Lichen-Covered Twig

has one spot of bright orange lichen

has one fat bud at its tip

close: Just the twig, with the lichen drawn in crinkly layers.
Only the tip of the twig, with the frilly lichen drawn large.

roles.light: for the pale edges of the frills
roles.accent: for the spot of orange lichen

close: Just the nest, seen from above, looking into the cup.
Only the nest, from the side, with the grass wound round and round.

roles.dark: for the hollow inside the cup
roles.light: for the pale dry grass on top
roles.accent: for the green moss woven in

phrases: more speckles at the wide end

close: Just the egg, life size, with each speckle dotted on one at a time.
Only the egg and the edge of the nest around it.

roles.dark: for the shadow side of the egg
roles.light: for the shine on the top
roles.accent: for the rusty brown speckles

firstMark: Start with the shadow on the egg's underside, a gentle crescent of {dark}.
Start with an even, light layer of {main}, leaving an oval of paper near the top for the shine.

title: The Blue Striped Feather
phrases: bright blue, black and white stripes
about as long as a thumb

is tucked into the band of an old straw hat
has a ruffled edge where it has split
is standing upright in a jam jar
is floating slowly down through the air

close: Just the feather, life size, with each blue and black stripe in place.

roles.dark: for the black stripes between them
roles.light: for the white stripes and the thin stem down the middle
roles.accent: for the fluffy grey-brown base

roles.accent: for the peachy pink inside the opening

title: The Ribbed Seashell
phrases: ribs running out from the top

has a neat round hole near the top
is holding a spoonful of water
is at the end of a row of smaller shells

roles.dark: for the grooves between the ribs
roles.light: for the smooth inside
roles.accent: for the rusty brown bands

is in a saucer with some blue and white pieces

roles.accent: for the bright green along the thin edges

has a round hole right through it
has a bit of blue rope tied round one end
has three pebbles balanced along its top

roles.light: for the palest ridges
roles.accent: for the warm brown deep in the cracks

firstMark: Start with the longest crack in the wood, one wavy line of {dark}.
Start with the grain in long strokes of {main}, following the twist of the wood.

has a sea snail on one branch

roles.accent: for the yellow-brown tips

roles.accent: for the green string round the stems

roles.accent: for the green leaves and stem

roles.light: for the pale creases in the petals
roles.accent: for the grey-green stem

roles.light: for the dusty pollen
roles.accent: for the tiny red buds on the twig

has turned yellow with brown tips
